en.sup: Supplied in English. The Aramaic names the groups first and takes them up again at the end with 'on them'.

01.r: Addresses the king's officials who receive the letter.

02.r: The king formally informs his officials.
02.n: Gesenius: in this form, to make known, to show. A participle with no pronoun: 'making known', with the king speaking as 'we'.

04.r: No one in these groups is left out.
04.n: BDB: the whole, all, and with a negative, none. Most translations say 'any of', since the sentence ends in a prohibition.

05.r: The priests serving at the temple in Jerusalem.
05.n: Gesenius: a priest, the Aramaic form of the Hebrew word, citing this chapter.

06.r: The members of the tribe of Levi who served at the temple.
06.n: Gesenius cites this verse for the plural, Levites.

07.n: Gesenius: a singer, citing this verse, the only one where the word occurs.

08.r: The guards of the temple gates.
08.n: Gesenius: a porter, door-keeper, citing this verse. In older English a 'porter' is a gatekeeper.

09.r: Assistants given to the Levites for the temple's work.
09.n: The Aramaic word is Nethinim, 'those given', as most translations keep it. The brief's lexicon: temple slaves assigned to the Levites and priests for service in the sanctuary.

10.r: Anyone else working in the temple's service.
10.n: A participle, 'those serving'. Gesenius: to labour, hence to serve, and specially to worship God. BDB lists priests and Nethinim among those who serve in this sense.

11.n: BDB: house, and of God, the temple at Jerusalem.

12.r: The God of Israel, as the Persian king names him.

13.r: Points to this temple, the one being restored.
13.n: The word comes after 'God' in the Aramaic, and the DRC reads it with God: 'the house of this God'.

14.r: The regular payment owed to the Persian king.
14.n: Our register renders this word 'tribute'. BDB: tribute; Gesenius treats it as the same word as another Aramaic word for tribute. The KJV and DRC put the three levies in a different order, calling this one 'toll'.

15.r: A second levy, kept apart from the tribute.
15.n: Our register renders this word 'duty'. Gesenius: a species of tribute, probably imposed on articles consumed, an excise, citing this verse. YLT has only two words for the three.

16.r: A third levy, charged on travel.
16.n: Gesenius: a way-toll, citing this verse; the brief's lexicon gives its root as the verb 'to walk'. Our register renders it 'road toll', keeping 'toll' for the Greek τέλος in the New Testament.

18.r: No official has the right to levy these payments.
18.n: An adjective, 'having power'. Gesenius cites this verse for the sense, followed by 'to' and a verb: there is power to do anything. The Geneva reads it as a person, 'no governour'.

19.r: To lay the levies on them.
19.n: The verb means to throw, to cast; Gesenius cites this verse for the sense 'to impose (tribute)'. YLT says 'to lift up'.

20.r: On the temple personnel named above.

_extra.19: μὴ (not): begins a clause in the Greek, 'let there be no tribute for you'.
_extra.20: ἔστω (let there be): part of the same clause.
_extra.21: σοι (for you): part of the same clause.

05.n: ἱερεύς, priest: the word our register renders 'priest' in the New Testament.

09.n: Ναθινίμ, the Hebrew name written in Greek letters.

10.n: λειτουργός, one who performs a public or sacred service. English 'liturgy' comes from this family of words.

14.n: φόρος, tribute: the word our register renders 'tribute' in the New Testament. The Greek has nothing for the duty and the road toll.

19.n: καταδουλόω, to enslave: the Greek says 'you shall not have authority to enslave them', where the Aramaic speaks of imposing levies.
